thread:
alex: Quick note — I'm proposing we add a 'priority brackets' feature to the backfill scheduler so small urgent recomputes can jump ahead of bulk non-urgent runs. Thinking 3 brackets: urgent (SLO-facing), high (product-facing), background (best-effort).
maya: That makes sense. Can you sketch how quotas would map? e.g., will urgent consume from a separate reserved pool?
tj: We should avoid a separate pool if possible; prefer weighted preemption + soft quotas so background jobs get a fair share but can be preempted by urgent.
alex: Initial idea: reserved capacity for 'urgent' at 10% of compute, high is weight 3, background weight 1. Preemption only allowed for urgent -> high/background, and high -> background.
sam: Console UX ask: we need to surface the bracket for each backfill job and estimated wait time and preemption risk. Product wants an 'SLO impact' badge when a job is marked urgent.
lee: Concern: preempting live Dedicated jobs will be messy. We must not steal slots from live online inference. This must only apply to reprocess/backfill fleet.
nina: For observability, we need per-bracket KPIs: queued time, preemption count, avg throughput, and cost estimate. Also a per-tenant history so we can detect abuse.
ops-bot: scheduler: submitted backfill job job-98321 by maya queued in bracket=high, est_start=2026-03-12T14:33:02Z
tj: Implementation detail: scheduler can tag jobs with bracket labels and add priority score = base_score + bracket_multiplier + recency_boost. Then we run a greedy bin-packing to pick jobs that fit the current slot window. Preemption = checkpoint + reschedule.
maya: Checkpointing is key. We need an operator runbook for resume semantics; ideally a resume token so customers don't lose progress.
lee: Also add a hard cap per-tenant to prevent a single tenant from occupying >30% of urgent capacity.
alex: Good call. Proposal: urgent_reserved_pct=10, tenant_urgent_cap_pct=30, high_weight=3, bg_weight=1, preempt_grace=90s.
sam: UI mock request: show the bracket selector in the backfill create flow, with a tooltip: "Urgent = SLO-facing, limited by reserved capacity; costs more." Also show a small cost delta estimate.
nina: Dashboard: add 'bracket heatmap' (time v. bracket v. queued_jobs) and an alert if urgent queue exceeds 2x throughput for 10m.
tj: On API semantics: POST /backfills accept field priority_bracket: "urgent|high|background". Server returns estimated_start and preemption_risk: "low|medium|high".
maya: For compatibility, default behavior should be background to avoid accidental urgent charges.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: config change queued for canary - backfill-priority-flags v0.1 -> staging
alex: Next steps: (1) proposal PR for scheduler defaults and tenant caps, (2) console mock + API schema, (3) runbook for operator resume + checkpoint tests. Can we aim for canary next week?
sam: I can take the console mock + tooltip copy.
tj: I'll pick up scheduler PR and simulation to validate fairness.
maya: I'll draft the runbook and checkpoint test matrix. Need a quick cost estimate — how much extra does 10% urgent reserved add to spend if used 100%?
nina: I'll add the dashboard panels and alerts to the observability board; will need sample metrics exported from the canary to fine-tune thresholds.
lee: I'll validate that Dedicated inference lanes are excluded from preemption path. If anything crosses infra boundaries we'll block.
alex: Awesome — please tag me on PRs and mocks. If we find edgecases in simulation we iterate.Thanks all.
